hints: Focus on how the size and polarising power of the Group 2 cation changes from $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ to $\text{Ba}^{2+}$.
Remember that a small, highly polarising $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion distorts the carbonate and nitrate ions more easily, so they decompose at lower temperatures.
Compare the two solubility trends: hydroxides become more soluble down the group, while sulfates do the opposite, so look for the one that falls.
walkthrough:
**Recall Thermal Stability Down Group 2**

Think of polarising power as how strongly the $2+$ ion pulls on electrons. $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ is small so it polarises strongly, $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ is large so it polarises weakly.

Stronger polarisation weakens the $\text{C-O}$ bond in carbonates and the $\text{N-O}$ bond in nitrates, so less heat is needed to decompose them:

**Apply To Carbonates and Nitrates**

This means thermal stability increases down the group. The temperature needed for decomposition therefore increases from magnesium to barium.
$$\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$2\text{M}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Recall The Two Solubility Trends**

Here is the lovely pair to memorise. Group 2 hydroxides become more soluble down the group, $\text{Mg}(\text{OH})_2$ is almost insoluble while $\text{Ba}(\text{OH})_2$ is quite soluble.

Group 2 sulfates do the opposite and become less soluble down the group, $\text{MgSO}_4$ is very soluble while $\text{BaSO}_4$ is insoluble.

**Pick The Decreasing Property**

Carbonate decomposition temperature increases, nitrate decomposition temperature increases, hydroxide solubility increases. Only sulfate solubility decreases from magnesium to barium.

options.A: Incorrect. Carbonates become more thermally stable down the group because the larger cation has lower charge density and distorts the $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ ion less. So decomposition temperature increases from Mg to Ba, not decreases.
options.B: Incorrect. For the same reason as carbonates, nitrates become more stable down the group. $\text{Mg}(\text{NO}_3)_2$ decomposes easily on heating while $\text{Ba}(\text{NO}_3)_2$ needs much stronger heating, so the temperature increases.
options.C: Incorrect. This is a common confusion between the two solubility trends. Hydroxide solubility increases down Group 2. $\text{Mg}(\text{OH})_2$ is sparingly soluble, $\text{Ba}(\text{OH})_2$ is much more soluble.
options.D: Correct. Sulfate solubility decreases down Group 2. $\text{MgSO}_4$ is soluble in water, $\text{CaSO}_4$ is sparingly soluble, and $\text{SrSO}_4$ and $\text{BaSO}_4$ are insoluble. This is the only property listed that shows a decrease from magnesium to barium.
